Here, the denominator is the imaginary number $3\text{i}.$ Note that this can be written as $0+3\text{i},$ so the conjugate is $0-3\text{i},$ or simply $-3\text{i}.$

So, we multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-3\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6-4\text{i}}{3\text{i}} & =\frac{6-4\text{i}}{3\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-3\text{i}}{-3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-18\text{i}+12{\text{i}}^{2}}{-9{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-18\text{i}+12(-1)}{-9(-1)} \\  & =\frac{-12-18\text{i}}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-12-18\text{i}}{9} & =-\frac{12}{9}-\frac{18}{9}\text{i} \\  & =-\frac{4}{3}-2\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
